mechanism_narrative: Accelerating GDP growth, as measured by the year-over-year change in real GDP, signals a strengthening economy that will boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Yield curve inverts (10y-2y < 0) within the next 6 months, indicating a looming recession that will negate the positive earnings signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in industrial production, as measured by the year-over-year change in the industrial production index, signals a supply shock that will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances following a sharp INDPRO drop, indicating the supply shock is not impacting equity prices as expected.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid rise in the unemployment rate, defined as an increase of more than 0.5 percentage points over the previous 3 months, signals a weakening labor market that will negatively impact consumer spending and drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Consumer confidence rises significantly (Conference Board index up > 5 points) in the month following the UNRATE trigger, indicating the labor market weakness is not impacting consumer sentiment as expected.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of falling housing starts and rising consumer sentiment signals a shift from residential investment to consumer spending that will boost S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Housing starts rise and consumer sentiment falls simultaneously over the next 3 months, indicating the predicted shift is not occurring.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the federal funds rate, defined as a rise of more than 0.5 percentage points over the previous 3 months, signals a tightening monetary policy that will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Equity market volatility (VIX) falls significantly (down > 20% from trigger level) over the next 30 days, indicating the monetary tightening is not impacting market risk perceptions as expected.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid acceleration in wage growth, as measured by the year-over-year change in average hourly earnings, signals a tightening labor market that will boost consumer spending and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Retail sales growth slows significantly (down > 2% year-over-year) in the month following the wage acceleration trigger, indicating the labor market strength is not translating into consumer spending as expected.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in the ISM manufacturing PMI, defined as a fall below 45, signals a contraction in the manufacturing sector that will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances following an ISM trigger, indicating the manufacturing contraction is not impacting equity prices as expected.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising consumer prices and falling consumer sentiment signals a squeeze on household purchasing power that will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Real consumer spending rises significantly (up > 2% year-over-year) in the month following the trigger, indicating the household purchasing power squeeze is not impacting consumption as expected.
